newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban fight back after Afghan troops advance.
newsitem.headline: Taleban fight back after Afghan troops advance.

text.p: Islamic Taleban rebels launched a fierce counter-attack against Afghan government forces on Monday to recapture part of the Kabul-Jalalabad road, a Pakistan-based Afghan news agency said.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said government troops had pushed the Taleban back from their frontline about 30 km (19 miles) east of the strategic town of Sarobi on Sunday.
A local Taleban commander, Abdul Razzaq, told AIP that his men had regained the lost ground in an early morning assault backed by tanks and artillery. Fighting was still continuing.
He said the Taleban had sent 20 tanks from the eastern city of Jalalabad towards Sarobi to support about 1,000 frontline fighters facing about 1,200 government troops in the area.
Razzaq said at least two of his soldiers had been killed in shelling on Monday. He had no figure for government losses.

He said the Taleban's top military commander, Mullah Borjan, was expected to move to the Sarobi front soon after mopping up government resistance in Kunar province on the Pakistani border, which fell to the rebels on Sunday.
No comment from the government side was immediately available and there was no independent account of the fighting.

The Taleban, who captured Jalalabad on September 11, have been tightening their grip on eastern provinces as part of their drive to take Kabul from forces loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani and impose strict Islamic law throughout Afghanistan.
